stories.title: Police Shoot Suspect in Sweden School Sword Attack: Several Injured
stories.summary:
A sword-wielding man attacked a secondary school in Sweden on Friday, resulting in one death and three injuries. The suspect was shot by police during the incident.

Swedish authorities confirmed that an 18-year-old male suspect was arrested after being shot. Initial reports indicated at least two people were seriously injured, while later updates specified one person killed and three others wounded.

stories.summary:
The Supreme Court has temporarily allowed the Trump administration to continue construction of a new White House ballroom. Chief Justice John Roberts issued an administrative stay on Friday, pausing a lower court injunction that would have halted above-ground work.

A federal district court had previously ruled that the project required congressional permission. The administration argued in response that the $400 million structure is necessary for national security purposes.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill two, officials say, a day after deadly attack on mall
stories.summary:
Russian strikes killed two people in Ukraine, officials said, a day after a deadly attack on a shopping mall. The new attacks followed an incident that left at least 16 people dead in what was described as a double-tap strike.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a “cowardly and deliberate” attack on a mall in Kryvyi Rih, his hometown. Al Jazeera reported the incident as part of a broader pattern of Russian drone strikes targeting civilian areas.

stories.title: UK, Canada and Australia condemn Israel for refusing criminal probe into aid worker killings in Gaza
stories.summary:
The United Kingdom, Canada and Australia have condemned Israel for refusing to conduct a criminal probe into the deaths of aid workers in Gaza. The three Western allies described Israel’s decision not to investigate as “shameful.”

The dispute centers on an Israeli strike on a World Central Kitchen convoy in 2024 that killed seven aid workers. Al Jazeera and BBC reports describe the governments’ criticism as part of broader diplomatic pressure over accountability for the incident.

stories.title: Why is the DOJ investigating Andreessen Horowitz’s board seats?
stories.summary:
The Department of Justice is reportedly investigating a potential antitrust issue involving Andreessen Horowitz, the venture capital firm. The probe centers on two a16z partners who hold board seats at companies that have since become competitors.

Ben Horowitz sits on the board of Databricks, while Martin Casado serves on the board of Fivetran. Although these firms were not necessarily direct rivals when a16z initially invested in them, their current competitive overlap has drawn regulatory attention.

The investigation is said to have been ongoing for nearly a year and involves the application of an 112-year-old antitrust statute that is rarely used against venture capital investors. The move highlights growing scrutiny over board conflicts of interest within the tech investment sector.

stories.title: More voices oppose Puerto Galera’s P50 environmental fee
stories.summary:
Opposition is growing in Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro, to a proposed P50 environmental user’s fee for Mindoro residents. Local figures and stakeholders are questioning the policy’s impact on tourism, fairness, and public consultation.

The measure under review is Municipal Ordinance No. 2025-030, also known as the Revised Puerto Galera Environmental User’s Fee System Ordinance.

It was passed in December, according to the Philippine Daily Inquirer.

stories.title: Senator asks US government watchdog to review how feds use hacking tools
stories.summary:
Senator Ron Wyden has requested a comprehensive review of how federal law enforcement agencies use hacking tools and spyware. The letter was sent to the U.S. federal watchdog.

The request specifically targets the FBI, DEA, ICE's HSI, and the Secret Service. Wyden is seeking clarity on how these tools are deployed against Americans.

stories.title: San Francisco-area estate sells for $70m in sign of AI-fueled wealth explosion
stories.summary:
A luxury Lake Como-inspired estate in the San Francisco Bay Area has sold for a record $70 million, marking one of the highest-priced residential transactions in Hillsborough.

The buyer is described as being involved in the AI industry, underscoring how artificial-intelligence-driven wealth is reshaping local real estate markets. The sale more than doubled the previous record price for the affluent town south of San Francisco.

The transaction highlights a broader trend of new tech millionaires entering the Bay Area housing market, pushing prices to extraordinary levels amid continued demand from high-net-worth individuals.

stories.title: Lobsters and acidic seas: can shellfish help neutralise one of the greatest threats to the ocean?
stories.summary:
Researchers are testing whether adding alkalis to seawater can help oceans absorb more carbon dioxide without harming marine life. The experiments focus on crustaceans such as lobsters, which are central to New England’s seafood culture and economy.

The work aims to address ocean acidification, a growing threat driven by rising CO2 levels. By making seawater less acidic, the process could potentially protect shellfish populations while also drawing down atmospheric carbon.

However, the research faces uncertainty after Trump halted funding for related projects. Critics warn that stopping this line of inquiry could delay practical solutions to one of the ocean’s most pressing environmental challenges.

stories.title: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol 2 review – once more unto the mercenary breach
stories.summary:
Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 has arrived on PC, Nintendo Switch/Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, bringing another three remastered titles from the stealth espionage franchise.

The collection revisits classic entries that have seen little change since their original releases. The Guardian's review notes a thematic disconnect between the games' narratives and modern realities.

Old Snake's claim in Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots that "war has changed" highlights this shift. Kojima Productions originally explored proxy wars fought by mercenaries without political stakes, but the current landscape differs significantly from those 2008 themes.

stories.title: Frustrated GP patients hang up as Yorkshire accent baffles AI receptionist
stories.summary:
Patients in South Yorkshire are reporting frustration with an AI GP receptionist that struggles to understand local accents, according to a health watchdog.

Healthwatch Rotherham said several practices in the area have introduced an automated assistant named Emma. The system is reportedly failing to process broad regional speech patterns, leading some patients to hang up during calls.

The AI company behind the chatbot claims it supports 17 languages. However, local health advocates say the technology remains ineffective for residents with strong Yorkshire dialects.
